events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry
Tortugas out 60 nm...

* Until 715 AM EDT.

* At 640 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 22 nm south of
Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving south at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight /100 AM MDT Sunday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 333 AM MST /433 AM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall through the day today. However,
downstream impacts will continue at Birdsprings through at least
this evening.
- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 3:00am MST /4:00am MDT/ the stage was 18.11 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels are expected forecast to fall below action
stage around 10:00am MST /11:00am MDT/ today.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State
Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf
develops.
